newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 31.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
All newspapers
LALOO YADAV DETAINED IN CORRUPTION SCANDAL

Laloo Prasad Yadav, former chief minister of Bihar, indicted in a multi-million dollar scandal was detained for a week by a special court. He was ordered held in judicial custody by Judge S.K. Lal until August 6 while federal police interrogated him in connection with the $280 million scandal.
The Economic Times
INDIA ASKS EUROPEAN UNION TO END BAN ON SEA FOOD

India wrote to the European Commission to reconsider its decision to ban marine products exports since most of the Indian companies met the European Union standards. India faces a total ban on seafood exports after the Veterinary Committee of the European Union recommended a ban on the imports of seafood items from India. If imposed, the ban will affect India's seafood export worth 15 billion rupees to the European Union.
LIQUID FUEL PUT UNDER SPECIAL IMPORT LICENCE

The government decided to put all liquid fuels for sanctioned power projects with a total capacity of 12,000 mega watt on the special import list. This is a departure from the earlier liquid fuel policy. The government will not allow liquid fuel based power projects beyond the sanctioned 12,000 mega watt. The offered policy incentives too are limited to those liquid fuel based power projects that were already sanctioned.
PIAGGIO TO GO ALONE WITH THREE-WHEELER PROJECT

Piaggio has parted ways with the LML company in the three- wheeler project and has decided to go ahead with it alone. Sources said there were differences between the partners over the viability of the project. Piaggio has decided to set up a factory in Maharashtra state. It will be set up by a separate Piaggio subsidiary to manufacture 4-stroke petrol and diesel vehicles. The investment details of the venture are being finalised. The LML decided to drop out of the project because it wanted to concentrate on the two wheeler business.
Financial Express
INDUSTRIAL BANK CUTS RATES ON DEBT INSTRUMENTS

The Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) slashed interest rates by one percentage point to two percentage points (100 basis points to 200 basis points) on debt instruments of all maturities. It also launched a band rate for instruments of one year and two year tenures. The IDBI now has the flexibility of paying a marginally higher interest rate within the stipulated band if a corporate is offering a higher quantum of funds.
Business Standard
$50 MILLION FLOOR FOR AUTO VENTURES LIKELY

Overseas passenger car ventures may have to bring in a minimum amount of foreign direct investment in equity capital. The lower limit is likely to be $50 million, sources in the Directorate General of Foreign Trade said. A minimum inflow of foreign funds is considered necessary since it will indicate the commitment of the overseas company to the venture. It is not clear whether this will be applicable or not to car ventures that are already operational or for which a memorandum of understanding has already been signed.
PROMOTERS' SHARE IN PUBLIC ISSUES MAY GO

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is planning to remove the mandatory contribution by promoters and lock-in within a public issue. SEBI said it would gradually phase out these two requirements. It has already limited the contribution by promoters in public issues of listed as well as unlisted companies at a uniform 20 percent irrespective of the issue size. There is a uniform lock-in period of three years on the promoters contribution.
The Observer
USED TYRE IMPORTS TO BE BANNED

The Commerce Ministry is planning to ban the import of used tyres following a recommendation by the Industry Ministry. The announcement is expected soon. The reasons for the ban is pressure from domestic tyre manufacturers and the possibility of large scale duty evasion. The Industry Ministry pointed out that no other country in the world allowed the import of old used tyres. It also felt that even brand new tyres could be imported by stating them to be used ones resulting in massive duty evasion.
FINANCE MINISTRY MAY HIKE TAX BY TWO PERCENT

The Finance Ministry is likely to increase the tax rate on the interest earnings by banks by two percent, banking division sources said. At present the tax rate is 20 percent. The ministry is also thinking of increasing various exemptions under the income tax net of the banks. The Finance Ministry proposal also suggests income tax concessions to investment in garments, leather and diamond-cutting industries. The aim of the tax rate increase is to mobilise more revenue from the banking sector.
